name: MARS sell hook burns pair reserves and syncs
summary: On every transfer into its MARS/WBNB PancakeSwap pair (a sell), the closed-source MARS token burns about twice the sold amount of MARS from the pair's own balance and calls sync() before the sold tokens arrive, so repeated sells ratchet the pair's MARS reserve down and its WBNB price up. The attacker flash-borrowed 350 WBNB, bought MARS in 1,000-MARS chunks through fresh receiver contracts and sold it back in 1,000-MARS chunks, triggering 195 burn-and-sync cycles, and left with the pair's WBNB.
notes: Reset is the token's deployment: the burn rate (slot 0x19) was 200 from the constructor and setBurnRate(220) only scaled it. An anvil replay of the anchor at block 37903299 drains the same 21.2 WBNB with slot 0x19 at 200, slot 0x18 (setOverFlowBurnAmount) at its earlier 1.5e24 or the mint counter slot 0xe at 2, and reverts with slot 0x19 at 0 or slot 0x17 at 10e18. Slot 0x17, 1,000 MARS at deployment, was lowered to 10 MARS by 0x7700d8cf (0x4bbc57f6) and restored to 1,000 MARS (0x7700d8cf at block 37901400) 95 minutes before the anchor; it reads as a per-transfer size cap (the attack traded in 1,000-MARS chunks) and the burn is about twice each sold amount, so a lower cap only multiplies the swaps needed (rule 8: changes loss size).

Campaign: every transaction in which the pair burned MARS three or more times (Etherscan MARS transfers to 0x0, blocks 37870000-latest): the anchor, a copycat in the next block (0x27055ae4 via 0x039e0dc8), the attacker's second run (0x2e4c71da), and 30 small multi-sell loops through contract 0x0a682be3 by eight EOAs. Before the anchor every user sell burned once; the two double-burn transactions (0x72a68a59, 0x6c5b5692) are aggregator split sells.
Loss is the pair's WBNB depletion over the campaign, the attackers' realised value (rule 12); the 1.09M MARS burned from the pair is not valued separately.
